4.title: Body Text Font
4.body:
## Feedback
"For accessibility, they need to be thicker/contrasting with the background. Thin fonts are in style for last few years which has been making them less accessible for people with low vision. If you wear any corrective lenses, it’s easy to test the visibility by looking around website without them. If you have a good vision, ask a friend or family! If letters all blend in with background, needs contrast/thickness. The visibility goal is to be able to recognize that there are texts there with blurry vision. You don’t have to be able to read them. (I can go on and on about this topic)"
\- Kai
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The body text font is a thicker sans-serif font.
   > Dyslexia-friendly fonts are preferred
- [ ] The body text font is darker to better contrast the background color.

13.title: Bump esbuild and @sveltejs/adapter-netlify
13.body:
Bumps [esbuild](https://github.com/evanw/esbuild) to 0.25.3 and updates ancestor dependency [@sveltejs/adapter-netlify](https://github.com/sveltejs/kit/tree/HEAD/packages/adapter-netlify). These dependencies need to be updated together. Updates `esbuild` from 0.24.2 to 0.25.3
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.25.3

  • Fix lowered async arrow functions before super() (#4141, #4142)

    This change makes it possible to call an async arrow function in a constructor before calling super() when targeting environments without async support, as long as the function body doesn't reference this. Here's an example (notice the change from this to null):

    // Original code
class Foo extends Object {
  constructor() {
    (async () => await foo())()
    super()
  }
}

    // Old output (with --target=es2016)
    
class Foo extends Object {
    
constructor() {
    
(() => __async(this, null, function* () {
    
return yield foo();
    
}))();
    
super();
    
}
    
}
    

    // New output (with --target=es2016)
    
class Foo extends Object {
    
constructor() {
    
(() => __async(null, null, function* () {
    
return yield foo();
    
}))();
    
super();
    
}
    
}

    Some background: Arrow functions with the async keyword are transformed into generator functions for older language targets such as --target=es2016. Since arrow functions capture this, the generated code forwards this into the body of the generator function. However, JavaScript class syntax forbids using this in a constructor before calling super(), and this forwarding was problematic since previously happened even when the function body doesn't use this. Starting with this release, esbuild will now only forward this if it's used within the function body.

    This fix was contributed by @​magic-akari.

  • Fix memory leak with --watch=true (#4131, #4132)

    This release fixes a memory leak with esbuild when --watch=true is used instead of --watch. Previously using --watch=true caused esbuild to continue to use more and more memory for every rebuild, but --watch=true should now behave like --watch and not leak memory.

    This bug happened because esbuild disables the garbage collector when it's not run as a long-lived process for extra speed, but esbuild's checks for which arguments cause esbuild to be a long-lived process weren't updated for the new --watch=true style of boolean command-line flags. This has been an issue since this boolean flag syntax was added in version 0.14.24 in 2022. These checks are unfortunately separate from the regular argument parser because of how esbuild's internals are organized (the command-line interface is exposed as a separate Go API so you can build your own custom esbuild CLI).

    This fix was contributed by @​mxschmitt.

  • More concise output for repeated legal comments (#4139)

    Some libraries have many files and also use the same legal comment text in all files. Previously esbuild would copy each legal comment to the output file. Starting with this release, legal comments duplicated across separate files will now be grouped in the output file by unique comment content.

24.title: [UI/UX] TitleAccessibility: Some buttons are unlabeled, making the app difficult to use for screen reader users
24.body:
Hello,
As a person who is blind, I use a screen reader to access digital interfaces, and audio cues to play video games. I've begun using RomM, and have found a few accessibility issues, mainly unlabeled buttons, and the interface seems very cluttered.

The first thing I've found is around where the GameM logo is, there are three buttons that do not have textual labels. After that is the search field. Then, the first list box, which I assume is for game systems, like SNES, Sega MegaDrive, ETC. If I press Enter on one, I hear "loading" but nothing seems to happen after that. If I Tab, I find another text field, which isn't labeled. If I Tab further, I find more unlabeled buttons, but also labeled items like "show matched" and "show unmatched." It seems to be a filtering system of some kind, but there aren't enough labeled controls to make this clear to me.

The biggest issue, though, is finding and playing a game. I pressed Enter on the Sega MegaDrive option in the systems list, and have found the following options: "US Flag Sega MegaDrive Link", "1 button link", "1 button link", "1 collapsed button link", in Tab order. It is unclear what any of those controls do, or what I should do I choose what I assume is a game, or game filter. However, I'll search for a game, Mortal Kombat 1.

I press the Game Logo link to go back to the home page, find the "search collection" edit field, and type the game name and press Enter. Below all the list boxes and controls are a few groups of controls: "Super Nintendo Entertainment system link", "1681 button link", "1681 Button link", and "1681 collapsed button link". Having explored a bit, I know the first numeric link downloads the ROM, and the second is the play button, and I guess the third is a menu button. So, if I press the second link, I can then Tab to the Play button and press Enter. Only to find that the game that opened was not the one I was looking for, which I didn't know because the game names weren't labeled with the name of the game.

So, I'm not sure what the developers of this repo know about accessibility, but if you'd like to make this more accessible, this site should help. https://www.w3.org/WAI/

Thank you so much for reading, and I hope this helps make emulation easier for everyone.

26.title: [1hr] Component: Card
26.body:
**Estimated Time to Complete:** 1 hour  
**Assignee:** @radodd  
**Status:** Pending prioritization (@JeremiahSecrist)

---

### Objective
Implement the `<Card />` component as an enclosed container with customizable padding, background scrim, and optional state layer. The component should support scaleFactor, variant, material, and optical correction adjustments.

---

### Requirements

- Create a functional React component using the provided structure and props.
- The component should render a `<div>` with `lk-component="card"`.
- Use `propsToDataAttrs` to map props into `lk-card-*` attributes.
- Support the following props:
  - `scaleFactor`: Controls padding and border radius based on font size, with values like `display1`, `body`, etc.
  - `variant`: "fill", "outline", or "transparent" (controls background behavior).
  - `material`: "flat", "glass", or "rubber" (controls backdrop-filter behavior).
  - `opticalCorrection`: "top", "left", "right", "y", "x", "all", "none" (fine-tunes internal offsets).
  - `isClickable`: Optional boolean (indicates whether the card should be interactive).
  - `children`: Optional content rendered inside the card.
- Apply styles according to the provided CSS spec, including the optical correction and material types.
- Ensure the component can accept any native HTML attributes via `...restProps`.

---

### Accessibility
The card should have visual and non-visual consistency. If the card is made clickable, ensure that proper interaction feedback (e.g., `aria-label`) is provided for accessibility.

---

### Notes

- If `isClickable` is true, the card should display a state layer to reflect interactivity.
- Ensure that the background scrim and visual effects do not interfere with readability or usability.

---

### References
Design: [Figma File](https://www.figma.com/design/O823ttOXKnldLvWuDCeNsh/LiftKit--Community-?node-id=0-9781&p=f&t=SzOzCoxaMo1VVomv-0)

30.title: Accessibility
30.body:
- [ ] Keyboard access to everything.  Notably there is no current way to tab out of the editor!  `accesskey` works, not sure how to make it discoverable.
  - [ ] Use HTML5 `<nav>` etc. to convey site structure.

The most central question is whether CodeMirror content is even visible to screen readers?
Even if yes, and even if it's is conveniently editable, it probably wouldn't hurt to serve initial content over HTTP to people/spiders without javascript, and to allow fallback to textarea/form submission (#7).
- [ ] Make sure HTTP body uses real structure e.g. `<h1>` and not just visual styling like `<span class="heading-1">`.
  - [ ] Specifically, use real `<a>` (or at least `<span href=...>`) links!  Important both for accessibility and link juice.
- [ ] Investigate also using real `<h1>` etc. within CodeMirror (via `renderLine` hook, with CSS overrides like `.CodeMirror .h1 { display-style: inline}`?).
  These is a harder problem that CM flattens logically nested structure like `# H1 *span* H1` into adjacent spans.  Probably acceptable(?).
- [ ] Long term: investigate a textarea adapter to Firepad.  Would allow switching to textarea (which is also desirable for spell checking) without losing real-time sync.  However, I'm afraid that replacing textarea content on incomping changes might be extremely distracting with screen readers. 

Another part is math.
- IIUC, MathJax is well accessible, as long as user can access its right-click menu.
- [ ] Use MathML (with SVG fallback?) in HTTP content.

There are surely other aspects...

Testing tools: http://www.wat-c.org/

43.title: Improve Form Handling, UI/UX, and API Integration for Complaint Submi…
43.body:
Summary:
This pull request addresses several improvements to the application, including bug fixes, UI/UX enhancements, and optimizations in API integration. The goal is to provide a better user experience, more reliable functionality, and cleaner code by refining state management, implementing better form handling, and improving the UI responsiveness.

**Changes Made:**
Bug Fixes:

- Corrected hardcoded Title and Body values in the complaint submission process.
- Fixed API endpoint usage by ensuring the correct URL concatenation for the savePath in the fetch request.
- Implemented the logic to update the complaints list after a new submission, ensuring the UI reflects the latest data.
- Reset form inputs (title and body) after successful submission to improve the user experience.

UI/UX Enhancements:

- Redesigned the complaint submission form and complaint cards for a more polished, user-friendly interface.
- Added loading indicators and disabled submit buttons during the saving process to provide users with clear feedback.
- Included error messages for failed submission attempts and required fields, improving form validation.
- Improved the layout and responsiveness of the complaint cards, making them more visually distinct and mobile-friendly.

Technical Improvements:

- Used useCallback for the fetchComplains function to optimize performance and prevent unnecessary re-renders.
- Implemented better accessibility practices by adding aria-required and associating label elements with form inputs.
- Typed all key state variables using TypeScript to ensure better type safety and consistency.
- Separated state management for loading, error, and save statuses, making the code more maintainable.

Technical Decisions:

- useCallback for Fetching: The useCallback hook was used to memoize the fetchComplains function, preventing unnecessary function recreations and improving performance when the component re-renders.
- Form Validation: Basic form validation was added to ensure that the title and body fields are not empty before submitting the complaint, preventing unnecessary API calls.
- UI Responsiveness: The CSS was optimized to make the layout mobile-friendly and visually distinct, with a focus on clarity and ease of use.
- State Management: Proper state management practices were employed to track the loading, saving, and error states, ensuring that the UI reflects the real-time status of operations.

### WCAG Information - WCAG Guideline Reference No: 2.4.6 Headings and Labels - WCAG version: 2.1 - WCAG level: AA ### Testing environment - MAC OS X - Chrome - ARC plugin ### Steps to reproduce - As a logged out user, open https://www.perlego.com/institutions/ - Use ARC plugin - Observe that there is an accessibility issues with the sliders: ### Issue explanation The error occurs because the embedded web player contains two sliders (role="slider") with identical or overlapping aria-label attributes: "Progress Bar" and "Volume (use up/down arrow keys to change)". While these labels are intended to describe separate controls, their implementation may lead to confusion for users of assistive technologies. ### Actual Behaviour Duplicate labels used Description: The form contains multiple fields with the same label text. WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion:AA [2.4.6 Headings and Labels External link](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG21/#headings-and-labels) frame: `
` html/body/div/div[7]/div[8]/div[2]/div/div[1]/div/div[1] _frame2: https://player.vimeo.com/video/1017638334?h=a95b910aactabindex: 0_ frame: ```
html/body/div/div[7]/div[8]/div[2]/div/div[2]/div/div/div[1]/div ``` _frame2: https://player.vimeo.com/video/1017638334?h=a95b910aactabindex: 0_ ### Expected Behaviour / Recommendation Recommendations 1. Provide Unique and Descriptive aria-label Attributes To ensure clarity, update the aria-label attributes to distinguish between the controls. For example: Progress Bar: html Copy code
Volume Control: html Copy code
2. Add aria-describedby for Additional Context For enhanced clarity, you can add aria-describedby to point to additional text descriptions that provide context. Example: html Copy code

Use left and right arrow keys to adjust the playback position.

3. Ensure Controls Are Clearly Separated Visually While this is primarily an accessibility issue, separating controls visually also helps reinforce clarity for all users. Summary of Fixes Assign unique and descriptive labels (aria-label) to each interactive element. Optionally, use aria-describedby to supplement labels with additional instructions or descriptions. Test the updated labels and descriptions with a screen reader (e.g., NVDA or VoiceOver) to ensure they are clear and usable. These changes will resolve the Duplicate Labels Used issue and ensure compliance with WCAG 2.1 Level AA.

65.body:
H_07 Title in page content correctly tagged is a direct violation of WCAG 1.3.1 Info and relationships. The title is a heading. It is not something else. Definitely not a P tag. 

It is the first heading that all other content relates to. Deciding that role mapping it to a P tag so that it is not distinguishable from any other body content seems beyond logic.

While I understand that assistive technology should correctly voice it as a title, the decision to map it to the most indistinguishable tag in the tags tree (a P tag) defies all logic.

69.title: Do not use `rowgroup` role for table body
69.body:
While [the `tbody` HTML element is _supposed_ to map to the `rowgroup` ARIA role](https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aam-1.0/#el-tbody), no browser implements this and this seems warranted because neither NVDA or JAWS can navigate by cell when a table’s body has a `rowgroup` role on it. Currently, [the Table pattern uses `role=rowgroup` for the table body](https://github.com/w3c/aria-practices/blob/6c304c5c66fdb86d5cf3f2c347d472aa922c71da/content/patterns/table/examples/table.html#L59). I think for now it should not and perhaps a note should be added. Whether we like it or not, developers do thoughtlessly copy these patterns without testing.

Cross-reference: https://github.com/w3c/html-aam/issues/474

[The ARIA spec for `rowgroup`](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria/#rowgroup) also calls out a spec issue related to this:

> NOTE
> This role does not differentiate between types of row groups (e.g., thead vs. tbody), but an issue has been raised for WAI-ARIA 2.0.

73.title: term: Accessibility
73.body:
I propose we change this term label to **Content accessibility** to be more specific about the type of accessibility we mean (e.g. content accessibility vs. wheelchair accessibility). This would also distinguish it a bit from the LoCS, thus we could consider our term a non-equivalent, exactly, and remove it from the overlapping terms list.

I would also propose using a limited number of examples in the definition (3 max) concerned with text, images, videos, and/or audio and _not_ any concerning presentational aspects alone (e.g. color contrast).

### References

In addition to the LoCS page as 1 reference (of the minimum 2 needed), another should be a source for web accessibility, and their are many standards bodies on this subject. Any other sources that focus on a given example used would be desirable too.

78.title: `<Text>` accessibility
78.body:
**Background** I often see people using the `variant` prop of the `` component to change the styling of a text element (as it is intended). However, without supplying an `as` prop, the `variant` changes the tag the element is rendered as, often having implications in the accessibility of the document. For example, it's easy to use some `title3` variant in order to get slightly emphasized text without the element having any semantic significance, but with the current defaults it gets rendered as an `

` and thus can screw up the heading tree of a page. **Suggestion** Similarly to "no aria is better than bad aria", I feel that we should render all `` components as `

` by default. Perhaps have some kind of an opt-in toggle for them to render as semantically significant elements if the tedium of manually specifying `as`-prop feels too big? I feel that in an ideal world things would work as they are currently, but I'm not sure what kinds of safeguards could be implemented to guide the users to correct patterns :thinking: **Other notes** Is there a reason that variants `body`, `bodySmall`, `bodyLarge` and `bodyStrong` are rendered as `` rather than `

`?

85.title: Popovers can be partially hidden in PF6
85.body:
With Patternfly popovers they can sometimes be hidden behind the sidebar or other components. Likely due to our iframe usage and clipping overall.

See comment here for more info.
https://github.com/cockpit-project/cockpit/pull/21611#issuecomment-2736245198

Snippet of @garrett's comment that is relevant:

> We have a few solutions:
> 
> 1. Fix the popover by **moving it in the DOM and using JS**: Reparent the popover outside of the clipping area, but this requires JS for positioning, which is a performance hit and doesn't work well. PatternFly-React has support for this.
> 2. Fix the popover with **CSS anchor positioning** (see https://css-tricks.com/css-anchor-positioning-guide/ and https://caniuse.com/css-anchor-positioning ) — sadly, this doesn't have full browser support yet. While this would be the ideal solution, _we can't really use this yet_ — unless we also use a polyfill: https://anchor-polyfill.netlify.app/ to provide a fallback support for Firefox and Safari (and Cockpit Client). Safari has this in their tech preview, and Firefox will probably add it within the year, so this polyfill is still needed for the next year or so.
> 3. Ensure the page content height takes up the **viewport height**, using either flex or grid. This doesn't actually fix the problem at all, but it provides more room for things to pop up within the content area.
> 4. **Don't scroll the rounded box**, but go back to scrolling the page, with something like:
>    ```css
>    .pf-v6-c-page__main,
>    .pf-v6-c-page__main-container, .pf-v6-c-page__drawer {
>      overflow: clip;
>    }
>    ```
>    ...while ensuring that body has overflow auto (at least vertically)... and probably making sure there's a gutter under the rounded content box too.
> 
> 1 - 3 do not address the usability and accessibility concerns, but fix the popover issue. 4 addresses the popover issue as well as the additional concerns, but deviates from the intended design of PatternFly 6 (which has these usability and accessibility issues baked in by default).
> 
> Due to the issues above, we need to let the PatternFly team know that this is a problem that clips needed content and introduces usability and accessibility issues, and hope that they address it accordingly.

91.title: [Autocomplete] Accessibility issues with keyboard navigation Autocomplete
91.body:
### Steps to reproduce

A) In Autocomplete, the Clear button is not accessible by keyboard. To reproduce:
1. Visit [Combo box example](https://mui.com/material-ui/react-autocomplete/?srsltid=AfmBOoow6C13-i92jh2hvdlccm30DWW7pWd_E09QJDiPA51stJqhRdHz#combo-box)
2. Select an option, then press tab

Expected: Focus moves to the now-visible Clear button
Current: Focus moves out of the example

My workaround:
```
slotProps={{
  clearIndicator: {
    tabIndex: 0,
    // In order to make the Clear Button focusable, disable the default behavior of hiding it except on hover
    sx: {
      visibility: 'visible',
    },
  },
}}
```
However, with this workaround, the clear button can only be activated with Space. Ideally, it would be activated with either Space or Enter.

B) In Autocomplete with Multi, pressing Enter when focused on a selected dropdown element causes the element to get deleted. To reproduce:
1. Visit [Multiple Values example](https://mui.com/material-ui/react-autocomplete/?srsltid=AfmBOooMMc3DR1oOQKTCPYW8_jUur1VWJ0LRJTPEhcvGh2942nSnIMGH#multiple-values), press Reset Focus button
2. Press Tab then down-arrow to open the combobox
3. Press Enter

Current: The selected option is deleted from the selection.
Expected: My expectation is that the dropdown would close, and the selected option would stay selected. (But perhaps this is intended behavior?)

C) In Autocomplete with Multi, when navigating with Voiceover, after deleting an option, focus returns to the document body. To reproduce:
1. Visit [Multiple Values example](https://mui.com/material-ui/react-autocomplete/?srsltid=AfmBOooMMc3DR1oOQKTCPYW8_jUur1VWJ0LRJTPEhcvGh2942nSnIMGH#multiple-values)
2. Enter an option or two.
3. Using VO, ctrl-option(or capslock)-left to select an option and delete.

Current: Focus shifts to the document body
Expected: Focus remains on the autocomplete component. (Perhaps this a bug with VO, not MUI?)

D) In Autocomplete with Multi, users should be able to tab around the selected options. To reproduce:
1. Visit [Multiple Values example](https://mui.com/material-ui/react-autocomplete/?srsltid=AfmBOoow6C13-i92jh2hvdlccm30DWW7pWd_E09QJDiPA51stJqhRdHz#multiple-values)
2. Select multiple options, then press shift-tab.

Expected: Focus moves to the option chips
Current: Focus moves out of the example. Option chips can only be focused using left-right arrows. Relates to other issues with chip accessibility https://github.com/mui/material-ui/issues/20470, but I think this is a separate problem specific to chips within Autocomplete.

### Current behavior

_No response_

### Expected behavior

_No response_

### Context

Hi MUI maintainers! While my team was auditing our app's accessibility, we came across a few things that we thought were accessibility problems within the Autocomplete component. Since we couldn't find existing issues for these, we wanted to create an issue to discuss with you. Let us know, which ones of these are desired behavior, which you'd consider bugs, and which may be fixed with the upcoming work on https://github.com/mui/material-ui/issues/25365!

I'll add the caveat that we are not screenreader users, ourselves.

This is my first time creating an issue in the MUI repo. Please let me know if anything else would be helpful. Thanks!

Related issues:
- https://github.com/mui/material-ui/issues/25365
- https://github.com/mui/material-ui/issues/20470 

### Your environment

Tested using examples in the current MUI docs (see links above), using VoiceOver on Chrome.

97.title: Add Menu for Changing Variables
97.body:
### Description
This issue suggests creating a user-friendly menu that allows users to easily change simulation parameters such as the gravitational constant, time rate, body mass, and trail length without needing to interact with sliders. The goal is to enhance the user experience by providing a more intuitive interface for adjusting these variables.

### Proposed Features
1. **Dropdown Menus**: Implement dropdown menus for selecting values for gravitational constant and time rate, allowing users to choose from predefined options.
2. **Input Fields**: Provide input fields for body mass and trail length, enabling users to enter specific values directly.
3. **Real-time Updates**: Ensure that changes made in the menu are reflected in the simulation in real-time, enhancing interactivity.
4. **Reset to Defaults**: Include a button to reset all parameters to their default values for convenience.

### Benefits
- Simplifies the process of changing simulation parameters.
- Improves accessibility for users who may find sliders cumbersome.
- Enhances overall user experience by providing a more organized interface.

### Additional Notes
- Consider the layout of the menu to ensure it fits well within the existing UI.
- Ensure that the new menu is responsive and works well on different screen sizes.
